newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-ELBER PLANS TO STEP INTO KLINSMANN'S SHOES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ELBER PLANS TO STEP INTO KLINSMANN'S SHOES.

text.p: VfB Stuttgart's Brazilian striker Giovane Elber intends to step into Juergen Klinsmann's shoes at Bayern Munich next season.

Elber made it clear on Thursday he planned to leave Stuttgart at the end of the season and replace Klinsmann who announced this week he was moving abroad because he was unhappy at Germany's richest but most controversial club.
Asked to comment about a recent campaign by Stuttgart fans to keep the Brazilian at VfB, Elber said: "I am very happy about this because it is proof that the fans recognise my performances.

"They know that I will give everything for Stuttgart until the last second. But in the summer I'm going...The miracle that some people are expecting won't happen. I am keeping to my word that I have given to Bayern."

Bayern and Stuttgart must now agree on the financial details of the 24-year-old forward's move. The Bavarians are believed to be ready to pay eight million marks ($4.8 million) to buy him out of his contract although Stuttgart want more.
Elber, who has scored 14 league goals this season in his unusual white boots, has played a major role in Stuttgart's championship campaign.

Bayern's attempts to attract a top-class striker to Munich took on even more importance on Thursday when another of their forwards, Marcel Witeczek, announced he was also leaving the club at the end of the season.
"The ways it looks I'm definitely going to Borussia Moenchengladbach," the 28-year-old forward said. "We just need to sort out a few details in the next few days."

Klinsmann, who had problems coping with the constant internal squabbling which is part of everyday life in Munich, gave more details on Thursday about why he decided to give up one of the most lucrative contracts in German soccer.

"I kept having talks with the club and noticed that I was having problems with my philosophy and character," the Germany captain said. "That it would be difficult to accept certain things in the future. That is why I made the decision.
"(Chairman) Franz Beckenbauer wanted me to end my career in Munich. He tried to persuade me to stay until the year 2000. But it didn't work out."

National team coach Berti Vogts said he was not surprised by Klinsmann's decision. He said he would not be too worried if Klinsmann even decided to move to the United States, a country which the forward is known to like.

"He is experienced enough to know where to go," Vogts said. "I would fly to Los Angeles to keep in contact with our captain. Of course I would be happy if he continued to play in one of Europe's top leagues."

Klinsmann has yet to decide where he will play next season but it will definitely be outside Germany. He is expected to receive offers from England where he had a successful season with Tottenham two years ago, as well as from Spain and Italy.
